chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The bound one does not lead the free, nor the one with paralysis lead the healthy, nor the one performing dry ablution lead those who have performed wudu, nor does the blind man lead in the desert unless he is directed towards the Qibla.'
And the prayer is not valid behind the Nāsib (one who opposes the Imams) with choice, he narred that.

key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: The Nāsib (one who opposes the Imams)
key_terms.الْمُقَيَّدُ: The bound one (e.g., by chains or debt)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions that disqualify a person from leading congregational prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the jurisprudential criteria for *imamah* (leadership in prayer), emphasizing that a leader must not be in a state of lesser ritual purity or physical capability compared to the congregation, such as one performing *tayammum* leading those with *wudu*. It further highlights the exclusion of the *Nāsib* (those who harbored enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt) as a valid Imam, linking physical and spiritual eligibility. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on both ritual perfection and doctrinal fidelity in the person leading the prayer.
